preamble: The shift from the voiced palatal nasal [ɲ] to the voiced velar nasal [ŋ] is a process of retraction or backing. It typically occurs as regressive place assimilation when a palatal nasal precedes a velar consonant, and as a historical change in Hakka and in the Goyaz Jê language Panará.

examples.note: Middle Chinese ɲ merged with ŋ in Hakka; Mandarin rén, Cantonese jan4.

Panará merged the nasal codas *m, *n, *ñ as ŋ. Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: ñ = [ɲ], j = [j ~ ʒ], c = [tʃ ~ tɕ ~ ts ~ c], ĵ = [dʒ ~ ɟ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ê/ô = close-mid [e]/[o], ṭʰ = aspirated alveolar stop, mb/nd = post-oralized nasals; a final ’ marks a coda without echo vowel, X // Y gives phrase-medial // prepausal allomorphs.
